A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAGPO and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Their corresponding methods, proofs, experiments, and supplementary material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAGPO benchmark results and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C, including per-task results in Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments, revises several comparisons, and adds a model-capacity experiment in Section 5.2 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The four-step guider–learner procedure, autoregressive guider, double clipping, masked KL constraint, and auxiliary learner objective remain unchanged. Explicitly stating parameter sharing and expanding the PMD background do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both appendices contain the same six suites and 43 agent/task configurations; the revised CoordSum and SMAX counts correct the main text. However, v2 specifies CoordSum target caps of 30, 50, 80, and 100, whereas v1 gives an adjustable maximum with a default but no task-specific overrides. Changed target coverage cannot be reliably distinguished from newly disclosed settings.

E2.justification: The main comparison replaces IPPO with HAPPO throughout Table 1 and the benchmark plots, substituting a sequential-update competitor for independent learning. This materially changes the comparison against alternative training paradigms. Figure 4(b) also adds CTDS reference curves to the alignment-ratio experiments.

E3.justification: The new capacity experiment varies decentralized actor widths from 2 to 128 on smacv2_5_units while retaining full-capacity centralized networks and critics. The existing benchmark protocol retains 20 million training steps, 122 evaluation checkpoints, and 32 evaluation episodes per checkpoint.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a focused capacity-sensitivity study comparing MAGPO, CTDS, and MAPPO. The existing guider, alignment-ratio, and auxiliary-loss analyses remain, with revised CoordSum curves and additional CTDS comparisons in the ratio analysis.

E5.justification: The established reporting remains ten seeds, bootstrap confidence intervals, and Table 1 means with standard deviations. However, the newly added capacity curves in Figure 6 show no error bars or confidence bands, unlike the other empirical curves. No increase in run counts is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds HAPPO results, removes IPPO results, and replaces all four CoordSum rows. For example, MAGPO/Sable means change from 117.06/131.75 on 5x20 to 157.61/48.35 on 5x20-80; comparable target settings are not established. Retained-method scores on the other 39 tasks are unchanged. New capacity findings are added, and reported CTDE/overall winning-task counts change from 33/19 to 32/20.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendix A add the weighted-Bregman PMD formulation and a derivation connecting it to the statewise objective. The monotonic-improvement theorem, sequential-update corollary, and their existing proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: centralized guidance aligned with decentralized learners, monotonic policy improvement, and competitive performance across 43 tasks in six environments. Revised winning-task counts and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds model-capacity mismatch as an applicability consideration and interprets the new experiment as robustness to deployment compression. It also changes the auxiliary RL loss from being described as critical to being less important than alignment ratio δ, while retaining its proposed counter-supervision mechanism.

D1.justification: Appendix B explicitly documents max_target and uniform target sampling. Tables 3 and 6 now document HAPPO configurations, Section 4.2 explicitly states learner parameter sharing, and Appendix C.3 revises tuning provenance without retaining v1's explicit restriction to tuning only MAGPO's extra parameters on existing tasks. The code/data access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds foundational references for natural policy gradients, Markov games, TRPO, PPO, and PMD, and removes the independent-learning reference associated with IPPO. The broader positioning relative to CTDE, CTDS, HARL, CTCE, and single-agent GPO remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and CTDS failure-mode exposition are substantially rewritten, the PMD background is expanded, evaluation and hyperparameter prose is reorganized, and the conclusion is shortened. Author/header text and citation style change, and acknowledgments and an LLM-use disclosure are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds the capacity plot, provides a visible Figure 2 legend and dashed CTCE curves, updates comparison legends, and replaces Table 1's colored highlighting with underlining. The per-task plot moves after Table 1 and becomes Figure 7. Existing multipanel arrangements largely remain within the new conference formatting.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a relevant HAPPO comparison and capacity-sensitivity evidence, improves PMD and CoordSum documentation, and better qualifies the auxiliary loss's importance. These are useful but limited gains: IPPO comparisons are lost, and the new capacity study lacks displayed uncertainty and a clear account of changing actor width at evaluation. The core method and original guarantees remain unchanged.
